key_drivers: The reaffirmed FY2026 adjusted-EPS guide of $3.85-$4.15 now requires an H2 that H1 has not earned. H1 FY26 adjusted EPS is $1.73 ($0.83 Q1 + $0.90 Q2) against $1.72 in H1 FY25 - up 0.6%. To reach the $4.00 midpoint, H2 must deliver ~$2.27 against ~$1.94 last year, roughly +17%. Q3 is the first quarter in which that step-up has to be visible, and the Nasdaq consensus of $1.01 is +23% on the $0.82 ABM actually earned in Q3 FY25

Margin is already conceding. At Q2 ABM beat on revenue (+8.4%, a record $2.3bn) yet reaffirmed rather than raised EPS, guided segment operating margin 'toward the low end' of 7.8-8.0%, and printed 7.3% against 7.9% a year earlier. A revenue-strong, margin-weak mix is precisely the shape that has produced ABM's guidance trims

The reaction history is heavily left-skewed: 6 of the last 8 prints closed down, mean absolute move 7.1%, computed from Yahoo daily bars (2024-09-06 -8.6%, 2024-12-18 -8.4%, 2025-03-12 -8.7%, 2025-06-06 -9.1%, 2025-09-05 +0.3%, 2025-12-18 -9.9%, 2026-03-12 -5.4%, 2026-06-05 +6.7%). Twice the stock opened up 4-7% and closed down 8-9%, so the damage came from the call rather than the release

September 2025 is the closest precedent and it is a warning: same quarter, ABM conceded FY25 EPS 'toward the low end of $3.65-$3.80'. It only escaped flat (+0.3%) because the stock had already fallen from $56 to $48. It has since recovered to $46.78 on the back of the Q2 rally, so less of that cushion is left

Against the call: Technical Solutions grew 27.2% and Aviation 19.5% in Q2, H1 new bookings were a record $1.2bn, and at ~11.7x the guide midpoint with analyst targets clustered $53-58 the stock is cheap enough that a plain reaffirmation could be taken well - which is exactly what happened on 2026-06-05
what_would_change_my_mind: A Q3 adjusted EPS at or above ~$1.00 with segment operating margin back at or above 7.8%, which would show the H2 ramp actually starting rather than being deferred into Q4 again.
reasoning: ABM's problem is arithmetic, not narrative. Management has reaffirmed $3.85-$4.15 twice while H1 grew adjusted EPS by half a percent, so the entire year is now parked in H2 and Tuesday is where the first instalment comes due. Revenue is not the issue - it is compounding at 8% with genuine strength in Technical Solutions and Aviation - but margin is running below plan and was already guided to the low end in June. The three outcomes are a clean beat that validates the ramp, another reaffirmation, or a trim toward the low end. Only the first is clearly good, and H1 does not support it. The base rate agrees: six of eight prints down, with two vicious intraday fades from up opens, which says the call rather than the release does the work. I hold this at Low certainty because coverage is thin (three estimates on the calendar), the last two prints broke the pattern, and an 11.7x multiple with $53-58 targets means a merely adequate quarter can still rally the stock.

key_drivers: This is the Q4 print, so the information that moves it is the first FY2027 framework, not the quarter. I can forecast the size of that reaction with some confidence and its sign with none - which is the whole reason for the abstention

Size is not in doubt. The last eight reactions, close before to close after, from Yahoo daily bars: +30.6%, +20.0%, +11.6%, -10.2%, +18.5%, -8.9%, +8.2%, -10.3%. Median 11.0%, mean 14.8%; the most recent four average 11.5%. On 2026-06-09 the stock gapped -18.8% and still closed -10.3%

The bull and bear cases are both intact and both sourced. Bull: adjusted EPS $0.77 in Q3 against $0.44, adjusted EBITDA +16.6% to $183m, net leverage 2.5x - the lowest since fiscal 2018 - guided FY26 free cash flow ~$330m against a $2.6bn market cap, and the Whole Foods primary-distribution contract extended to May 2032, which removes the overhang that used to define this name. Bear: sales fell 4.2% in Q3 and missed, management narrowed rather than raised, and the optimization actions are not lapped until Q1 FY2027, so the first FY27 revenue line will show another decline

The two prior Q4 prints were both large up-moves (+30.6% on 2024-10-01, +18.5% on 2025-09-30), but both came from far more depressed setups - $31.76 into last September's. At $43.76 the stock has re-rated ~38% year on year and sits essentially on the $45 analyst median (range $38-56), so the low-bar mechanism that produced those two moves is much weaker now
The drift into the print is mildly supportive but not a signal: -8.6% over the past month and -21% over three, with no company-specific news I could find behind it
what_would_change_my_mind: An FY2027 adjusted EBITDA or EPS framework that grows off the FY26 $685-705m base despite the revenue decline would make this a Lean Up; a framework that flattens EBITDA while sales fall again would make it a Lean Down.
reasoning: I can see what this print turns on and I cannot call it. UNFI is deliberately shrinking - Q3 sales fell 4.2%, roughly 450bp of it self-inflicted network optimization - while profitability climbs hard: adjusted EPS $0.77 against $0.44, EBITDA +16.6%, leverage down to 2.5x. Tuesday sets the first FY2027 frame for that trade-off, and the market has taken it both ways at extreme size, alternating between +18.5% and -10.3% over the last four quarters. The two precedents that look most like Tuesday, the prior two Q4 prints, were both huge up-moves, but both started from a beaten-down stock; today's has re-rated to the analyst median and the optimization drag runs through Q1 FY27, so I do not think that precedent transfers. A directional call here would be dressing up a coin flip, and in the backtest this method made its money by not doing that. The magnitude number is the part I stand behind: low double digits, on a base rate of 11-15%.
